title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
disposition_detail: Specifications 1 and 5 and the appeal were sustained. Specifications 2–4 were moot. Presbytery’s judgment was reversed in whole, and all charges and specifications against the Session were dismissed.
first_summary: A Session appealed Presbytery’s judgment finding it guilty and suspending it for refusing instructions to institute process against a member. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed the judgment in whole, and dismissed the charges because Presbytery continued the matter after denying the member’s complaint and did not follow the required BCO 40-5 procedure. The remaining allegations concerning delay, prejudice, and a missing witness were moot.
summary: A Session appealed Presbytery’s judgment finding it guilty and suspending it for refusing instructions to institute process against a member. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed the judgment in whole, and dismissed the charges. Once Presbytery denied the member’s complaint, that matter should have ended; moreover, Presbytery did not follow BCO 40-4’s required first step before invoking BCO 40-5 review and control. The delay, prejudice, and missing-witness specifications were moot. The decision did not fault Presbytery’s underlying concern.
